text:
Leo Carlsson is having the season the Ducks drafted him second overall for. He's 21, playing 20 minutes a night, and Anaheim has handed him the power play: he's on the ice for 89% of its man-advantage time, up from 68% last season. The result is 26 points in 19 games, 18 of them with the extra man.

That's a real breakout in role, and role is the part that sticks. The scoring rate is a little ahead of itself. He's shooting 18.8% against a talent range near 14%, and his 4.05 points per 60 sits well above the 3.1 our numbers think he's capable of over a full year. At five on five, Anaheim gets under half of the expected goals with him on, though it's better than when he sits.

Last season he was the opposite story: Evolving-Hockey had him creating 2.4 expected wins but only 1.1 actual, the chances there and the finishing not. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries, an elite rate. Watch his even-strength scoring as the power play cools. That will tell you how big this jump is.
headline: Carlsson has the keys now
